unresolvedReferences.description: Duan Chaoyong's favor and the regency proposal are undated in the text (c. 1540 inferred).
Dismissal of Luo Hongxian, Zhao Shichun and Tang Shunzhi is undated (c. 1540 inferred).
Xu Xuemo and Wu Zongzhou's resistance is dated only as after 1561.
The English table of contents misassigns the generational headings; extraction follows the Chinese headings.
Yi Liu's enfeoffment 'at age four' is computed as c. 1571.
Chang Fen's memorials during the Chongzhen bandit crisis are undated.
Lü Weiji's warning to Chang Xun is undated (c. 1640 inferred).
Chang Hao's age 25 without a consort is not tied to a year.
Chang Hao's flight to Chongqing with Hou Liangzhu is undated (before 1644).
Wang Zhiming and Lady Tong's claims are dated only as 'before long' after 1644.
Chang Run and Chang Ying unmarried at twenty: year not given.
Zhu Youlang's enfeoffment as Prince of Yongming is dated only to the Chongzhen era.
Deaths of Chang Ying's heir and of Prince Anren are undated.
The Prince of Ji is not named personally in the text.
Years 五年/六年/八年 follow the Shunzhi count (1648/1649/1651); the English draft mislabels them as Yongli years.
Yan Qiheng's killing dated 1651 per text (八年 counted from the chunk's sequence); exact year uncertain.
Years 九年/十五年/十七年/十八年 follow the Shunzhi count (1652/1658/1660/1661); English draft mislabels them as Yongli years.
'Two years later' and 'the following year' are dated by inference (c. 1654-1657); Sancha battle c. 1657.
Birth and death years of the infant princes and of the Tianqi sons and all listed consorts are not given.
The former Prince of Min's son is unnamed and not extracted as a person.
Zhu Cihuan's death at age five is not dated in the text (c. 1640 inferred).
Li Huang's memorial is undated (c. 1640 inferred).
The Chongzhen Emperor's seventh son is unnamed and undated; not extracted.
Wang Bing (Wang Zhiming's alleged grandfather) is named but not offered as a candidate; not extracted.
Birth and death years of the three Tianqi crown princes are not given.
